newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Perth airport master plan in a year, manager says.
newsitem.headline: Perth airport master plan in a year, manager says.

text.p: Perth Airport is poised for a healthy growth pattern for up to 20 years, a spokesman for the airport's winning bidder Airstralia Development Group (ADG) said on Wednesday.
ADG would put together a long-term master plan over the next 12 months for the airport and saw Asia as one of its key growth markets, spokesman Ryne Johnson told a news conference.

"It is an area that is experiencing rapid growth into Perth right now but we would by no means limit our expectations to Asia as a growth market," Johnson told the conference, held after the Australian government's announcement of the winning
bidders for the Perth, Melbourne and Brisbane airports.

ADG is a mainly Australian-owned consortium comprising international airport operator Airports Group International (AGI) with 16 percent, infrastructure investment company Infratil Australia Trust with 49 percent and the Australian Airport Property Fund with 35 percent.
AGI is a subsidiary of Lockheed Martin Corp.
Johnson said AGI has international experience as both an airport operator and developer with major airport facilities at Trillium Terminal 3 in Toronto and Atlanta International Airport.
Perth Airport handles over four million passengers and over 30,000 tonnes of international air freight a year.
ADG bid A$643 million for the lease and also gave the Western Australia state government a commitment to reduce aeronautical charges by 25 percent in real terms over the next five years.

ADG managing director George Casey said in a statement the group had bid for Perth out of the three on offer "on the basis of the quality of the asset and the value we believe ADG can add to the airport, the city of Perth and the State as a whole".

Johnson said the long-term plan would consider whether to merge the airport's domestic and international operations in one complex as well as the commercial development of the airport site, including its retail potential.
"There is no question about it that the retail segment of the airport will be a fundamental part of making this business venture successful," Johnson said.
